meta.title: Nuclear fuel supply chains for Tamil Nadu reactors (Kudankulam, MAPS, PFBR) + Indian fuel-cycle facilities
notes: Coordinates only where OSM/Wikipedia/GEO give them; many UCIL mines/mills have no public coordinates and are left null (never guessed).
loc_precision: exact_osm | wikipedia | co-located_approx (placed on a neighbouring sourced feature) | campus_approx | adjacent_site_approx | town_centroid | null.
Transport modes for uranium concentrate, fuel bundles and plutonium are security-sensitive and unpublished: mode "unknown" is used rather than inventing rail/road.
Kudankulam fuel arrives by chartered cargo aircraft from Russia (Dec-2025 unit-3 delivery); the Indian airport is not named in any source found.
npcil_units table in data/power.db was checked: it has no Kudankulam rows and garbled capacity columns, so it was not used.

nodes.name: Kudankulam Nuclear Power Project (KKNPP) units 1-6
nodes.status: U1-2 operating (2 x 1000 MW VVER-1000/V-412); U3-4 commissioning (first fuel delivered Dec-2025); U5-6 under construction (2021)
nodes.notes: Light-water VVER: needs enriched UO2 fuel (imported from Russia) but no heavy water.
sources: https://world-nuclear.org/information-library/country-profiles/countries-g-n/india (World Nuclear Association, Nuclear Power in India; raw/feedstock/nuclear/wna_india.html)
CEA/NPP Daily Generation Report in data/power.db table dgr_stations (2026-09-22): KUDANKULAM 2000 MW, MADRAS A.P.S. 440 MW, BHAVINI PFBR 0 MW

nodes.name: Madras Atomic Power Station (MAPS), Kalpakkam
nodes.status: operating: 2 x 220 MW-class PHWR (205 MWe each in WNA reactor table; units critical 1983 & 1985)
nodes.notes: Natural-uranium PHWR, heavy-water moderated & cooled, seawater-cooled condensers. NOT under IAEA safeguards (India's 2006 separation plan), therefore fuelled only with domestic (UCIL) uranium.
sources: CEA/NPP Daily Generation Report in data/power.db table dgr_stations (2026-09-22): KUDANKULAM 2000 MW, MADRAS A.P.S. 440 MW, BHAVINI PFBR 0 MW

nodes.name: Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR), Kalpakkam
nodes.status: first criticality 6 Apr 2026 (Wikipedia); not yet in commercial operation (DGR 0 MW)
nodes.loc_note: OSM node 6861924154 (power=generator); Wikipedia 12.55306,80.17333.
nodes.notes: Pool-type sodium-cooled FBR; MOX (PuO2-UO2) driver fuel, U (and planned Th) blanket; 1,750 t sodium. India will not accept safeguards on PFBR or FBTR (IPFM 2014).
sources: https://world-nuclear.org/information-library/country-profiles/countries-g-n/india (World Nuclear Association, Nuclear Power in India; raw/feedstock/nuclear/wna_india.html)

nodes.name: Fast Breeder Test Reactor (FBTR), IGCAR Kalpakkam
nodes.loc_note: Wikipedia coordinates.
nodes.notes: Mixed-carbide fuel from BARC; its spent fuel reprocessed at IGCAR (CORAL, DFRP) - closes the fast-reactor fuel cycle at small scale.
sources: https://world-nuclear.org/information-library/country-profiles/countries-g-n/india (World Nuclear Association, Nuclear Power in India; raw/feedstock/nuclear/wna_india.html)

nodes.name: TVEL / Rosatom uranium conversion & enrichment (specific plant not published)
nodes.loc_note: Which Russian enrichment plant supplies KKNPP fuel is not published.
sources: https://world-nuclear.org/information-library/country-profiles/countries-g-n/india (World Nuclear Association, Nuclear Power in India; raw/feedstock/nuclear/wna_india.html)

nodes.name: Novosibirsk Chemical Concentrates Plant (NCCP / NZKhK)
nodes.loc_note: OSM way 51916722 "Новосибирский завод химконцентратов".
nodes.notes: Fabricates the TVS-2M VVER-1000 fuel assemblies delivered to Kudankulam (unit-3 first core Dec-2025; units 1-2 on TVS-2M since 2022, 18-month cycles).

nodes.name: Indian arrival airport for KKNPP fuel flights (not published)
nodes.loc_note: Press releases say the assemblies "were flown by cargo plane" (7 flights for unit-3 core + reserve) but do not name the airport.

nodes.name: KKNPP on-site spent-fuel storage (in-reactor pools + away-from-reactor store)
nodes.status: storage; reprocessing planned in a future safeguarded Indian plant
nodes.loc_note: On the KKNPP site; footprint not mapped.
nodes.notes: 1988 agreement required return of used fuel to Russia; 1998 supplement allows India to retain and reprocess it under safeguards (WNA).
sources: https://world-nuclear.org/information-library/country-profiles/countries-g-n/india (World Nuclear Association, Nuclear Power in India; raw/feedstock/nuclear/wna_india.html)

nodes.name: UCIL Jaduguda uranium mine (underground, since 1967)
nodes.loc_note: Wikipedia Jaduguda Uranium Mine coordinates; OSM town node Jaduguda 22.65563,86.34995.
nodes.notes: Ore grade ~0.05-0.06% U (WNA). Singhbhum shear zone, East Singhbhum dist., Jharkhand.
sources: https://world-nuclear.org/information-library/country-profiles/countries-g-n/india (World Nuclear Association, Nuclear Power in India; raw/feedstock/nuclear/wna_india.html)

nodes.name: UCIL Jaduguda mill (processing plant)
nodes.loc_note: Placed at the Jaduguda mine coordinates - Wikipedia: "Jadugoda process plant is located close to the mine".
nodes.notes: Treats ore from Jaduguda, Bhatin and Narwapahar; product magnesium diuranate (MDU, "yellowcake").
sources: https://world-nuclear.org/information-library/country-profiles/countries-g-n/india (World Nuclear Association, Nuclear Power in India; raw/feedstock/nuclear/wna_india.html)

nodes.name: UCIL Tummalapalle uranium mine (YSR Kadapa, AP)
nodes.loc_note: OSM way 963431375 "Tummalapalle uranium mine" (landuse=quarry); Wikipedia 14.32,78.26.
nodes.notes: Resources ~120,229 tU (2017, WNA) - India's largest deposit. Commercial production from June 2012.
sources: https://world-nuclear.org/information-library/country-profiles/countries-g-n/india (World Nuclear Association, Nuclear Power in India; raw/feedstock/nuclear/wna_india.html)

nodes.name: UCIL Tummalapalle mill (alkaline pressure leach)
nodes.loc_note: Placed at the mine; exact mill footprint not separately mapped.
nodes.capacity: 3,000 t/day expanding to 4,500 t/day (WNA); expected ~220 tU/yr
nodes.notes: Produces sodium diuranate.
sources: https://world-nuclear.org/information-library/country-profiles/countries-g-n/india (World Nuclear Association, Nuclear Power in India; raw/feedstock/nuclear/wna_india.html)

nodes.name: Nuclear Fuel Complex (NFC), Hyderabad (Moula Ali/ECIL area)
nodes.loc_note: OSM way 356190914 "NFC Guest House" (campus vicinity; plant footprint not mapped); OSM "DAE Colony" 17.46994,78.56899; Wikipedia Moula Ali 17.468,78.556.
nodes.notes: Refines MDU/SDU to UO2, makes pellets, zircaloy tubes and 220 MWe PHWR fuel bundles (15.2 kg UO2 each, Wikipedia) - MAPS fuel comes from here. Some NFC facilities are safeguarded (for imported uranium), others are not.
sources: https://world-nuclear.org/information-library/country-profiles/countries-g-n/india (World Nuclear Association, Nuclear Power in India; raw/feedstock/nuclear/wna_india.html)

nodes.name: Heavy Water Plant Tuticorin (HWB)
nodes.status: operating per HWB list (Wikipedia: one of seven plants; also makes solvents)
nodes.loc_note: OSM way 309279889 "HWP"; OSM "Hwp Township Hospital" 8.73568,78.12104 nearby.
nodes.notes: Commissioned July 1978; monothermal ammonia-hydrogen exchange, historically integrated with the neighbouring SPIC ammonia plant. The only HWB plant in Tamil Nadu.

nodes.name: Heavy Water Plant Manuguru (Aswapuram)
nodes.loc_note: OSM way 109386335 "Aswapuram Heavy Water Plant".
nodes.notes: Bithermal H2S-H2O exchange; flagship HWB plant (Dec-1991); captive 3 x 30 MWe coal power plant.

nodes.name: Heavy Water Plant Kota (Rawatbhata)
nodes.loc_note: OSM way 175347138 "Heavy Water Plant".
nodes.notes: H2O-H2S bithermal; next to RAPS.

nodes.name: Heavy Water Plant Baroda (Vadodara)
nodes.status: heavy-water production suspended 1999 (GSFC ammonia plant change); potassium metal plant
nodes.loc_note: Placed at OSM way 29547338 GSFC (HWP is "adjacent to GSFC").

nodes.name: Heavy Water Plant Hazira
nodes.loc_note: "about 16 km from Surat city" (Wikipedia); no sourced coordinate.
nodes.notes: Ammonia-hydrogen exchange, commissioned Feb-1991.

nodes.name: Heavy Water Plant Thal (Thal-Vaishet, Raigad)
nodes.loc_note: Placed at OSM way 122091071 RCF Thal fertiliser complex (host plant).
nodes.notes: Commissioned 1985.

nodes.name: Heavy Water Plant Talcher
nodes.status: heavy-water production suspended 1994; now solvent (D2EHPA, TBP) and B-10 enrichment facilities
nodes.loc_note: Wikipedia Talcher town coordinates (plant not mapped).

nodes.name: Kalpakkam Atomic Reprocessing Plant (KARP), BARC Facilities Kalpakkam
nodes.status: operating (commissioned 1998; shut 2003-2009 after an accident, upgraded)
nodes.loc_note: IGCAR/Kalpakkam campus coordinates (Wikipedia IGCAR); KARP footprint not mapped.
nodes.notes: Reprocesses MAPS spent fuel (BARC 2003). Supplies plutonium for FBR fuel.
sources: https://fissilematerials.org/library/barc03.pdf (P.K. Dey, BARC, "Spent fuel reprocessing: an overview", INSAC-2003; raw/feedstock/nuclear/barc03_spent_fuel_reprocessing_overview.pdf)

nodes.loc_note: Placed at OSM way 331427518 Tarapur Atomic Power Station (BARC Tarapur campus adjoins; facility footprint not mapped).
nodes.notes: Reprocesses unsafeguarded PHWR fuel (KAPS per BARC 2003).

nodes.name: BARC Advanced Fuel Fabrication Facility / Fuel Fabrication Facility (MOX), Tarapur
nodes.loc_note: Same campus placeholder as PREFRE (OSM TAPS site).
nodes.notes: Fabricates PFBR MOX fuel; BARC director (Jan-2023): 100,000 fuel elements made for PFBR.
sources: https://world-nuclear.org/information-library/country-profiles/countries-g-n/india (World Nuclear Association, Nuclear Power in India; raw/feedstock/nuclear/wna_india.html)

nodes.name: IGCAR CORAL / Demonstration Fast Reactor Fuel Reprocessing Plant, Kalpakkam
nodes.loc_note: IGCAR campus (Wikipedia).
nodes.notes: Reprocesses FBTR carbide fuel.

nodes.name: Fast Reactor Fuel Cycle Facility (FRFCF), Kalpakkam
nodes.loc_note: Kalpakkam; site coordinates not published/mapped.
nodes.notes: Will reprocess PFBR spent fuel and re-fabricate fuel to close the PFBR cycle (WNA).
sources: https://world-nuclear.org/information-library/country-profiles/countries-g-n/india (World Nuclear Association, Nuclear Power in India; raw/feedstock/nuclear/wna_india.html)

steps.notes: Chartered cargo aircraft; unit-3 initial core + reserve needed 7 flights (Dec-2025 onward).
Final leg by road assumed (no rail/sea link to the fuel store is reported); airport not named.
Retained in India; to be reprocessed in a future safeguarded plant.

chains.notes: Units 1-2: TVS-2M since 2022 (18-month cycles). Unit 3 is the first VVER-1000 to start on an 18-month cycle; 2024 contract covers units 3-4 for life. No heavy water needed.
sources: https://world-nuclear.org/information-library/country-profiles/countries-g-n/india (World Nuclear Association, Nuclear Power in India; raw/feedstock/nuclear/wna_india.html)

chains.fuel_type: natural UO2 (220 MWe PHWR fuel bundles, 15.2 kg UO2 each)

steps.notes: Bhatin and Narwapahar ore is processed at Jaduguda (Wikipedia UCIL); mode not published.
mill assignment not stated explicitly; Turamdih mill "serving these mines" (WNA)
Road transport likely but not documented.
Same Kalpakkam complex; MAPS spent fuel reprocessed at KARP (BARC 2003).

chains.heavy_water: Moderator/coolant D2O from the Heavy Water Board pool (plants: Tuticorin, Manuguru, Kota, Hazira, Thal, Baroda, Talcher). Which plant supplies MAPS make-up is not published; HWP Tuticorin is the only one in TN.
chains.notes: Mill-to-reactor shares are not published (UCIL output is not disclosed). Wikipedia's MAPS article says spent fuel went to Tarapur reprocessing "since 1985"; BARC (2003) assigns MAPS fuel to KARP (commissioned 1998) - both may be true for different periods.
sources: https://world-nuclear.org/information-library/country-profiles/countries-g-n/india (World Nuclear Association, Nuclear Power in India; raw/feedstock/nuclear/wna_india.html)
https://fissilematerials.org/library/barc03.pdf (P.K. Dey, BARC, "Spent fuel reprocessing: an overview", INSAC-2003; raw/feedstock/nuclear/barc03_spent_fuel_reprocessing_overview.pdf)

chains.fuel_type: MOX (PuO2-UO2) driver fuel; depleted/natural U (and later Th) blanket
chains.supplier: BARC (Pu recovery + MOX fabrication at Tarapur)

steps.notes: Plutonium from existing PHWRs (WNA); inter-site transport not published.
Assumed U source for MOX & blanket (NFC makes UO2 pellets incl. depleted U); not explicitly documented for PFBR.
Tarapur -> Kalpakkam (~1,300 km); mode not published.
Future: FRFCF to close the cycle.

chains.notes: Core loading began 4-Mar-2024 (initiated), final loading from 18-Oct-2025, first criticality 6-Apr-2026 (Wikipedia).
